gh issue comment 147 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
The premise holds -- `cppcheck`, `clang-tidy`, `scan-build` and `clang`
are all absent here, and CI installs only `libncurses-dev` and `tmux` --
but one line of it needs correcting before it misleads whoever picks
this up.

> `gcc -fanalyzer` has been used as a substitute by hand in several
> passes, and is closer, but nothing asks for it.

The substitute those passes actually ran was
`gcc -fanalyzer -fsyntax-only`, and **it analyses nothing**.
`-fsyntax-only` stops before the analyzer passes run. Measured:

```c
#include <stdlib.h>
int main(void) {
	int *p = malloc(sizeof(int));
	free(p);
	return *p;			/* use after free */
}
```

```
$ gcc -fanalyzer -fsyntax-only fa.c ; echo "exit $?"
exit 0

$ gcc -fanalyzer -c -o /dev/null fa.c
fa.c:5:16: warning: use after 'free' of 'p' [CWE-416] [-Wanalyzer-use-after-free]
```

So those runs were not a weaker check than the real thing; they were no
check, reported as clean. That makes the gap this issue describes wider
than it says, and it is the reason the fix below builds a canary into
the test rather than trusting a clean run.

**cppcheck cannot be verified on the development machine.** There is no
root here, and the extracted `.deb` will not run: the binary has
`FILESDIR` compiled in and refuses to start without
`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/cppcheck/cfg/std.cfg`, which cannot be
placed without root. `--library=` does not get past it either. So the
first suggested fix would have meant shipping a check nobody here could
execute -- visible only when CI ran it, which is the shape of gap this
issue is about. `gcc -fanalyzer` runs here and on Linux CI.

**The codebase is clean under it, with one false positive.**
`setup.c:662` read `quad[ix][iy]` where `ix`/`iy` are set only inside a
loop over `klhere`, and the analyzer cannot carry `quadnum >= 100` down
to `klhere >= 1` across the thirty lines between them. The invariant
does hold -- `klhere` is `quadnum/100` and `quadnum` does not move in
between -- so it is not a bug. The line now names the same square the
way the line under it already does, `quad[kx[klhere]][ky[klhere]]`,
which needs no such argument to read.

Review the user-facing behaviour of the change on branch `chore/static-analysis` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. Read AGENTS.md and .claude/agents/ui-review.md.

**State:** no commits (HEAD `1ff91fe` = `main`); modified `setup.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `.claude/agents/verifier.md`; new untracked `tests/analyze.sh`.

## What it does

Issue **#147**. `verifier.md`'s step 2 asked for `cppcheck`, `clang-tidy` or `scan-build` "if installed" — none of the three is installed here or in CI, so that leg of verification never ran anywhere, on any machine. The change makes it real with `gcc -fanalyzer`, as a `tests/analyze.sh` in the ctest suite.

**Only one line of game code changed, and that is what I want you on.** `setup.c`'s `newqad()` promoted a Klingon to commander with

```c
quad[ix][iy] = IHC;
```

where `ix`/`iy` are set only inside the loop over `klhere` above it. `gcc -fanalyzer` reported a read of uninitialized `ix`. It is a false positive — `klhere` is `quadnum/100`, the block is gated on `quadnum >= 100`, and `quadnum` does not move in between, so the loop always runs — but the line now names the same square the way the line *below* it already does:

```c
quad[kx[klhere]][ky[klhere]] = IHC;
```

After the loop, `ix`/`iy` are `kx[klhere]`/`ky[klhere]` — the last Klingon dropped in — because the loop's final iteration assigned them. So it should be the same square in every game.

**That "should" is what I want checked.** This is the square a commander appears on in the short-range scan, so if I am wrong the player sees a `C` in the wrong place, or a Klingon that never became one. `golden`, `tournament`, `journey` and `score` all pass unchanged, which is decent evidence — the golden recordings are the only thing in the suite that checks the game's arithmetic — but they cover a fixed set of seeds.

Please drive games that actually contain a commander and compare what the scan shows against a build of `main`:

- tournament seeds with a commander in the starting quadrant, and quadrants entered later that hold one;
- the `C` on the short-range scan, and that the count of Klingons plus commanders is unchanged;
- a game where the commander's quadrant holds exactly one Klingon (`klhere == 1`), which is where the "last Klingon dropped in" is also the only one;
- anything that would show a commander sitting on top of another object, or a square that should have been empty.

The rest of the diff is a test script, a `CMakeLists.txt` entry and the `verifier` brief — none of it runs while the game runs.

Same constraints: private tmux socket via `-L <yourname>` with `-f /dev/null`, never a bare `kill-server`, never `kill-session` on a session you did not create, scratch directory with a copy of `sst.doc`, never redirect the game's stdout in the pane.

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
ctest --preset ci-debug 2>&1 | tail -2
git add -A && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
test(ci): make static analysis a check that actually runs

verifier.md's step 2 asked for cppcheck, clang-tidy or scan-build "if
installed". None of the three is installed on this machine or in CI, so
that leg of verification never ran anywhere, on any machine, while every
pass reported the gap honestly and the gap stayed open.

tests/analyze.sh runs gcc -fanalyzer over the sources the game is built
from, with -Werror so any diagnostic fails. It skips where no compiler
offers -fanalyzer and fails rather than skipping on Linux CI, which is
the idiom tests/tui.sh already uses for tmux.

Two things turned up while building it.

gcc -fanalyzer -fsyntax-only analyses nothing. Several passes had
reported it as a clean substitute; it exits 0 on a blatant use-after-free
where -fanalyzer -c catches it. Those runs were not a weaker check but
no check, reported as clean. So the compiler is chosen by compiling a
deliberate use-after-free: one that takes the flag and reports nothing
is passed over rather than trusted.

cppcheck could not be verified here at all -- no root, and the extracted
package will not start without a std.cfg that cannot be placed. Choosing
it would have meant shipping a check nobody here could execute, which is
the shape of gap this closes.

The flags, the compiler and the source list come from CMakeLists.txt
rather than being written out again. The first version restated them and
had already drifted, analysing as C23 where every preset compiles gnu17.

setup.c's commander promotion was quad[ix][iy], which the analyzer read
as uninitialised. A false positive -- klhere is quadnum/100 and the
block is gated on quadnum >= 100 -- but the line now names the same
square the way the line below it already does, kx[klhere]. ui-review
instrumented 150 games: 123 promotions, no mismatches, and 96 A/B games
byte-identical against a main build.

What the check does not buy is uniform depth. gcc's reach is per
function, not per file: the same planted read is caught in newqad() and
phasers() and missed in cramen(), tui_shutdown() and cloak(). The
thresholds that recover them, and the fact that nothing reddens at 12,
are measured in the script's comment and on #171.

ui-review skipped for everything after its one round: comments, the test
script, CMakeLists.txt, README.md and the brief, none of which the game
prints. verifier ran three times, code-review seven.

Closes #147
